To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the brain microsomes from the different regions of the rat brain have a significant ability to metabolise xenobiotic substrates and that the activity of P450s in the brain microsomal fraction is inducer specific.
The O-dealkylation reactions in brain are inducer selective and substrate selective.
the dealkylation of 7-alkoxyresorufins by rat brain microsomal cytochrome P-450s (P-450s) is inducer specific, and that this is due to the induction of P-450 isoenzyme(s) in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of cytochrome P-450 isoenzyme(s) in the rat central nervous system.
the characterisation of P450 isozymes and their regulation in the brain.
the characterization of the xenobiotic (drug) metabolising P450 isoenzyms in brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the brain microsomes contain at least two forms of P450 isozymes, one of them being a P450 1 isozyme and the other being a P450 II isozyme, which can catalyze the O-dealkylations of alkoxy-resorufin derivatives.
the O-deethylation of ER in brain microsomes is catalysed by P450 1 family, while the O-dealkylations of BR and PR are catalysed by both P450 1 and 2 families.
P450 1a1 and 2B1 are present in rat brain microsome and the activity of P450 3A is also present but at a very low level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dealkylation of 7-alkoxyresorufins, which is isoenzymespecific in rat hepatic microsomes is also specific in rat brain microsome.
the brain microsomes are capable of catalysing the dealkylation of the alkoxyresourfins and that the activities of PROD and EROD are inducer specific, while the activity of BROD is inducer specific.
, the P450 2A1/1B1, P450 1B2 and P450 2C6 are present in the rat brain microsomal fraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain microsomes can be used as an in vitro model to study the role of xenobiotic metabolism in the central nervous system.
the brain has its own set of xenobiotic P450s that are different from the hepatic P450s.

the dealkylation of the three alkoxyresurufins can be a useful tool to characterise P450s in brain and other tissues and that the dealkylase activity is inducer selective and isoenzyme dependent in rat brain.
